sources.note: No phonology content for Pannei. The Pannei paragraph (pp. 6-7 of the article) gives only location, speaker estimate, religion, status as a separate language with internal dialect/external relation studies still to be done, and lexical-similarity diagrams; the only phonological remark in the subfamily section is that PUS dialects show 'not only lexical variation but also phonological'. No stress, accent or tone statement anywhere in the article (scanned text searched: stress/accent/penult/tone absent).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi (Pacific Linguistics D-78). Canberra: ANU. viii+216 pp.
sources.note: Only a blanket symbol note in Appendix E (p.93): 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists.' Tapango (= Pannei) is listed as PUS dialect f. WITHOUT the asterisk that marks 'word list included in Appendix E' (Fig. 5, pp.16-17; description p.41), so no Pannei data underlie the statement.
